newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares backtrack ahead of 1997 Budget.
newsitem.headline: KL shares backtrack ahead of 1997 Budget.

text.p: Profit-takers reaped gains in Kuala Lumpur stocks ahead of the unveiling of Malaysia's 1997 Budget on Friday after boosting prices earlier this week on expectations of a market-friendly blueprint, dealers said.

"They're profit-taking in case they get caught by any negative surprises," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp. But, she added: "So far all the figures floating around indicate a further consolidation of the economy, which is a good thing."
The blue chip-focused Composite Index ended down 1.22 points to 1,177.13.
Secondary stocks, which gained sharply this week, were sold down more than blue chips. The Second Board index dropped 10.13 points or 1.61 percent to 619.72.
A dealer at a local firm said investors appeared to be taking a more cautious attitude just prior to the Budget.
"There were not many orders coming in today. But quite a number of investors think the Budget will be favourable. I don't see anything to be worried about," she added.
Incentives to promote the high-technology, transportation, and education sectors are expected to be in the Budget. Analysts say a 1-2 percent corporate tax cut is also possible.
